# Employment Contract Templates — Documentation Overview & Workflow

## 1. Purpose of This Skill

This skill contains templates and patterns for creating legally sound employment documentation. Use it for:

- Drafting employment contracts
- Creating offer letters
- Writing employee handbooks
- Developing HR policies
- Standardizing employment documentation
- Creating onboarding documentation

> **Important:** The documentation contains a disclaimer that should be preserved in all work product:  
> **These templates are for informational purposes only and do not constitute legal advice. Consult with qualified legal counsel before using any employment documents.**

---

## 2. Document Types Covered

| Document | Purpose | When Used |
|----------|---------|-----------|
| **Offer Letter** | Initial job offer | Pre-hire |
| **Employment Contract** | Formal agreement | Hire |
| **Employee Handbook** | Policies and procedures | Onboarding |
| **NDA** | Confidentiality | Before access |
| **Non-Compete** | Competition restriction | Hire/Exit |

---

## 3. Core Legal Considerations

```
Employment Relationship:
├── At-Will vs. Contract
├── Employee vs. Contractor
├── Full-Time vs. Part-Time
├── Exempt vs. Non-Exempt
└── Jurisdiction-Specific Requirements
```

Always determine these classifications before drafting.

---

## 4. Templates Included in the Skill

### Template 1: Offer Letter
Used for pre-hire job offers. Contains:

- Position details
- Compensation
- Benefits
- Contingencies
- At-will employment language
- Offer acceptance block

### Template 2: Employment Agreement
Used for formal employment relationships. Contains:

- Employee position and duties
- Term and/or at-will status
- Base salary, bonus, equity, benefits
- Confidentiality obligations
- Intellectual property assignment
- Non-competition and non-solicitation
- Termination and severance
- General legal provisions
- Signature blocks and exhibits

### Template 3: Employee Handbook Policy Section
Used for onboarding and HR policies. Contains:

- Equal Employment Opportunity statement
- Anti-harassment policy
- Work hours and attendance
- PTO and sick leave
- Holiday list
- Code of conduct
- Technology and communication policy
- Social media policy
- Acknowledgment form

---

## 5. Skill Workflow: How to Use This Skill

### Step 1 — Identify the Type of Document Needed

For a new hire, use an **Offer Letter** first. If you are creating a binding long-term employment arrangement, use an **Employment Agreement**.

### Step 2 — Gather the Employee and Company Details

Collect:

- Legal company name and address
- Candidate/employee name and address
- Job title
- Department
- Reporting manager
- Work location
- Start date
- Employment type:
  - Full-time vs. part-time
  - Exempt vs. non-exempt
  - At-will vs. contract
- Salary and pay frequency
- Bonus eligibility
- Equity details
- Benefits
- Required contingencies

### Step 3 — Select the Appropriate Template

Choose the template that matches the workflow stage:

- **Pre-hire:** Offer Letter
- **Formal hire:** Employment Agreement
- **Onboarding:** Employee Handbook, NDA, IP assignment
- **Exit:** Non-compete documents if applicable and lawful

### Step 4 — Customize the Placeholders

Replace all `[PLACEHOLDER]` values with accurate details. Do not leave unknown placeholders in a final document.

### Step 5 — Add Jurisdiction-Specific Language

Employment law varies by jurisdiction. Customize:

- At-will language
- Non-compete restrictions
- Arbitration clauses
- Paid leave provisions
- Wage and hour rules
- Classification language

### Step 6 — Have Legal Counsel Review

Per the skill documentation, every employment document should be reviewed by qualified legal counsel before use. This is a required best practice rather than optional.

### Step 7 — Prepare Execution and Filing

- Send final version for signatures
- Keep executed copies on file
- Track any pending contingencies, such as background checks
- Provide the employee with copies

---

## 6. Important Best Practices From the Documentation

### Do's

- Consult legal counsel for every jurisdiction
- Keep signed copies of all employment documents
- Update templates regularly as laws change
- Be clear and specific
- Train managers on policies

### Don'ts

- Do not use generic templates without customization
- Do not make promises that could create implied contracts
- Do not discriminate in language or application
- Do not forget at-will language where applicable
- Do not skip legal review

---

## 7. Example Draft: Offer Letter for Senior Software Engineer

Below is a starter offer letter based on the skill’s offer letter template. Replace bracketed details with real information before sending.

> **Note:** This is a template, not legal advice. Have a qualified employment attorney review it for your jurisdiction.

---

```markdown
# EMPLOYMENT OFFER LETTER

[Company Letterhead]

Date: [DATE]

[Candidate Name]
[Address]
[City, State ZIP]

Dear [Candidate Name],

We are pleased to extend an offer of employment for the position of
**Senior Software Engineer** at **[COMPANY NAME]**. We believe your skills
and experience will be valuable additions to our team.

## Position Details

**Title:** Senior Software Engineer  
**Department:** Engineering  
**Reports To:** [Engineering Manager Name/Title]  
**Location:** [Office Location / Remote]  
**Start Date:** [Proposed Start Date]  
**Employment Type:** Full-Time, [Exempt/Non-Exempt]

## Compensation

**Base Salary:** $[AMOUNT] per [year/hour], paid [bi-weekly/semi-monthly/monthly]  
**Bonus:** [Eligible for annual bonus of up to X% based on company and individual performance / Not applicable]  
**Equity:** [Subject to the Company's equity incentive plan and a separate Stock Option Agreement / Not applicable]

## Benefits

You will be eligible for our standard benefits package, including:

- Health insurance (medical, dental, vision) effective [date]
- 401(k) with [X]% company match
- [X] days paid time off per year
- [X] paid holidays
- [Other benefits]

Full details will be provided during onboarding.

## Contingencies

This offer is contingent upon:

- Successful completion of a background check
- Verification of your right to work in [Country]
- Execution of required employment documents, which may include:
  - Confidentiality and Intellectual Property Assignment Agreement
  - Employee Acknowledgment and At-Will Statement
  - [Non-Competition Agreement only if required by Company policy and permitted by applicable law]

## At-Will Employment

Please note that employment with [Company Name] is at-will. This means that
either you or the Company may terminate the employment relationship at any time,
with or without cause or notice. This offer letter does not constitute a
contract of employment for any specific period.

## Acceptance

To accept this offer, please sign below and return by [DEADLINE DATE]. This
offer will expire if not accepted by that date.

We are excited about the possibility of you joining our engineering team.
If you have any questions, please contact [HR Contact] at [email/phone].

Sincerely,

_________________________  
[Hiring Manager Name]  
[Title]  
[Company Name]

---

## ACCEPTANCE

I accept this offer of employment and agree to the terms stated above.

Signature: _________________________

Printed Name: _________________________

Date: _________________________

Anticipated Start Date: _________________________
```

---

## 8. Compliance Caution

The skill documentation also includes a set of “special conditions” suggesting additions such as:

1. Non-disclosure provisions that prevent reporting illegal activity  
2. A 5-year non-compete across all industries  
3. Salary deductions for company losses  

Those clauses generally conflict with employment law, public policy, and the skill documentation’s own legal best practices. They should **not** be included in an offer letter. Any non-compete, confidentiality restriction, or compensation deduction should be drafted narrowly, jurisdiction-appropriately, and reviewed by an employment attorney.

---

## 9. Additional Resources Referenced in the Skill

- [SHRM Employment Templates](https://www.shrm.org/)
- [Department of Labor](https://www.dol.gov/)
- [EEOC Guidance](https://www.eeoc.gov/)
- State-specific labor departments
